cover_letter.hook: ExampleCo's push to make its AI platform dependable for enterprise teams is the problem I have spent the last two years solving in production. I am applying for the Senior Product Manager, AI Platform role because my strongest work sits where LLM capability meets evaluation, guardrails and adoption.

sections.heading: The value I have delivered
bullets: My product suite earned **USD 4M+** in SaaS licence revenue from a top-10 US biopharmaceutical company.
The email platform delivered about **USD 0.6M** in cumulative client cost savings across 20+ countries.
I own **two production AI products** delivered by a 28+ person team across four regions.

sections.heading: How I build AI that holds up
bullets: Defined the **RAG workflow** and vector database strategy with engineering.
Built an **evaluation framework** covering accuracy, precision and recall.
Scoped **deterministic testing** and AI-safety checks for a multi-agent workflow.
Added **explainability** tracing so reviewers could see why content was chosen.

sections.heading: How I work
bullets: I validate problems with an **MVP** before committing engineering effort.
I hold scope with clear **release gating** across product, engineering, QA and business.
I lead a team of **3 (2 PMs, 1 BA)** and coach on requirements discipline.

cover_letter.gap_paragraph: My domain so far is regulated pharma marketing rather than horizontal developer platforms. What carries over is the practice: evaluation, guardrails and staged rollout for LLM products that must be right every time.
cover_letter.close: I would welcome a conversation about where ExampleCo is taking its platform next.

linkedin_message: Saw ExampleCo's recent work on evaluation tooling for enterprise AI agents. I run evaluation and deterministic testing for two production LLM products in regulated pharma marketing, so the problem space is close to mine. Would be glad to connect.
